name: Landscaper
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for landscaper businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Landscapers operate heavy equipment and vehicles across outdoor properties, giving the trade meaningful property-damage and equipment exposure similar to other outdoor trades.

riskFactors.title: Property Damage from Equipment
riskFactors.description: Mowers, trimmers, and other power equipment can damage irrigation lines, fences, or hardscaping during routine work.

riskFactors.title: Vehicle & Trailer Accidents
riskFactors.description: Landscapers transport heavy equipment and materials between properties daily, creating commercial auto exposure.

riskFactors.title: Debris & Equipment Injury
riskFactors.description: Flying debris from mowers or trimmers and injuries from power equipment are common sources of bodily-injury claims.

faqs.question: Why do landscapers need Commercial Auto insurance?
faqs.answer: Trucks and trailers used to haul equipment and materials between job sites for business purposes generally require Commercial Auto rather than a personal auto policy.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a landscaper?
faqs.answer: A landscaper in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $330 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Does General Liability cover damage to a client's sprinkler system?
faqs.answer: Yes, accidental damage to irrigation systems or other property during routine landscaping work is a typical General Liability claim.

faqs.question: What does an equipment floater cover for a landscaper?
faqs.answer: It covers mowers, trimmers, and other equipment against theft or damage while being transported or stored away from a fixed business location.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Landscapers carry a 1.65 actuarial risk factor, reflecting heavy equipment use, vehicle transport, and outdoor property-damage exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, crew size, and Commercial Auto or Equipment Floater endorsements.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Landscaping premiums are comparable to handymen and painters, reflecting moderate-to-high physical and equipment risk below licensed trades like electrical or HVAC work.
